## BOOK 1 of 2: "Strong Poison" by Dorothy L. Sayers (Gutenberg 78157, © 1930)

**Epigraph:** Old ballad "Lord Rendal" ("Where gat ye your dinner...", "strong poison").

**Main characters**
- Harriet Vane: novelist of detective stories, age 29, on trial at the Old Bailey for murdering Philip Boyes with arsenic. Dark square brows, dark smudgy eyes, deep voice. Former lover of Boyes; brought up religious; orphaned/left at 23.
- Philip Boyes: 36, writer of "advanced" novels (atheism, free love). Curly hair worn long. Son of Rev. Arthur Boyes (Vicarage at Tweedling Parva). Dies 23 June 1929 at Norman Urquhart's house, Woburn Square.
- Lord Peter Wimsey: amateur sleuth, monocle, "Mrs. Merdle" = his car; man = Bunter; sister Lady Mary Wimsey; mother = Dowager Duchess of Denver; brother Gerald, Duke of Denver; wife Helen.
- Chief-Inspector Charles Parker (Scotland Yard).
- Sir Impey Biggs: defence counsel. Attorney-General (prosecutor). Judge (old, parrot-faced; later plump, eighteenth-century face at verdict stage).
- Mr. Crofts of Crofts & Cooper: defence solicitor.
- Hon. Freddy Arbuthnot: Wimsey's friend.
- Miss Katharine (Kitty) Climpson: spinster, juror, runs "The Cattery" typing bureau; letters signed "Katharine Alexandra Climpson".
- Salcombe Hardy, Waffles Newton, Cuthbert Logan: press reporters.
- Norman Urquhart: solicitor, cousin of Boyes, Woburn Square / office Bedford Row. Freckled, sleek dark hair, ~mid-40s.
- Hannah Westlock: parlourmaid. Mrs. Pettican: cook.
- Dr. Grainger, Dr. Weare: doctors. Sir James Lubbock, Stephen Fordyce: analysts.
- Nurse Williams: nurse who gossiped.
- Ryland Vaughan: Boyes' friend; Sylvia Marriott, Eiluned Price: Harriet's friends; Joey Trimbles; Marjorie Phelps (porcelain figurine maker); Nina Kropotky (Bohemian party).
- Mr. Challoner: Harriet's literary agent. Mr. Cole of Grimsby & Cole (publisher of Boyes); Mr. Trufoot (Harriet's publisher).
- Joan Murchison: Wimsey's operative as clerk in Urquhart's office (Miss Murchison). Mr. Pond: head clerk. Mrs. Hodges: charwoman.
- Bill Rumm ("Blindfold Bill"): ex-cracksman, now locksmith/preacher; wife Bella; daughter Esmeralda Hyacinth.
- Cremorna Garden / Rosanna Wrayburn: actress, great-aunt of Urquhart and Boyes, Windle, Westmorland; paralysed, ~93.
- Miss Caroline Booth: nurse to Mrs. Wrayburn. Mrs. Craig: spiritualist. Pongo: "control". Fedora: Mrs. Craig's control.
- Mrs. Bulfinch (née Montague, "Gracie"): barmaid at the Nine Rings, Grays Inn Road; husband George Bulfinch.
- Miss Tweall, Mrs. Pegler, Miss Etheredge, Mrs. Liffey: Hillside View boarding-house residents, Windle.
- Marjorie; "Bunter" (Wimsey's manservant, photography room).
- Dr. Dixon Mann / Valetta cited as authorities.

**Timeline (Harriet/Boyes)**
- 1927: they meet. March 1928: Harriet consents to live with him.
- Feb 1929: quarrel; Boyes offered marriage (Harriet felt "made a fool of"). Harriet leaves; flat at 100 Doughty Street. Boyes goes to Woburn Square (Urquhart's).
- Meetings: late March, second week April, some time May.
- 10 April 1929: Harriet buys 2 oz commercial arsenic at Mr. Brown's chemist, Southampton Row, signed "Mary Slater". Also prussic acid, strychnine; aconitine attempt. Explains: novel "Death in the Pot" (galleys later). 
- 5 May: arsenical weed-killer, signed "Edith Waters" (Kidwelly poisoning case brand).
- Boyes' gastric attacks: 31 March, 15 April, 12 May (Dr. Weare's case-book). Also earlier 1925.
- Harlech trip with Vaughan. 16 June letter to Harriet ("Life is an utter mess-up... trip out West... I shall be in town on the 20th"). Her reply: "You can come round at 9.30 on the 20th... not make me change my mind." Signed "M."
- 19 June: Boyes back to town with Vaughan. 20 June: bacon/eggs breakfast; Guinness at 11; lunch at club; tennis.
- 20 June dinner at Urquhart's, 8 o'clock: sherry (Oloroso 1847, poured by maid); cold bouillon (Hannah served); turbot with sauce; poulet en casserole; sweet omelette made by Boyes in chafing-dish with four eggs (one cracked, Urquhart bought, asked it be used) and hot jam; Boyes alone drank Corton Burgundy (2 glasses; bottle sealed, preserved, found harmless; Hannah put plaster and initials on bottle).
- 9.15 Boyes leaves in taxi; 9.25 arrives Doughty Street (PC D.1234 witnessed). Mrs. Bright ground-floor resident. Harriet offered coffee "standing ready on the gas-ring" / "in the fender"; prior statement "I had a cup of coffee ready for him".
- ~10 pm Boyes says he'll leave, feels unwell. 10.10 taxi (driver Burke) from Guilford Street rank to Woburn Square; "Yes, rotten." Hannah gave brandy-and-soda. Urquhart: "God knows!... It can't have been the chicken."
- Dr. Grainger; mixture (bicarbonate of potash, tincture of oranges, chloroform). Dr. Weare consulted 21 June.
- Death 3 a.m. 23 June 1929. Funeral 28 June. Last words: "I'm going out, Dad... Harriet'll be rid of me now."
- Nurse Williams gossiped (last week June) → Vaughan → Urquhart → Dr. Weare → Rev. Boyes → police; exhumation.
- Analysis: ~4–5 grains arsenic taken ~3 days before death; hair arsenic near roots (~3 months); no charcoal/indigo found.
- Harriet's flat searched; no poisons found. She said she destroyed poisons before end of May.
- Challoner: book about poisoning discussed since December.

**Trial structure:** Ch I–II prosecution & summing-up by judge; jury out 6.5 hours; disagreement. Ch III: Wimsey claims innocence; Miss Climpson stood firm for acquittal. Ch IV: council (Crofts, Sir Impey); Wimsey visits Harriet in Holloway, proposes ("forty-seven proposals"). Ch V: Miss Climpson's office; Wimsey visits Scotland Yard; Parker; "My Cattery." Ch VI: Rev. Arthur Boyes at Tweedling Parva; will leaving copyrights to Vaughan; earlier will to Harriet; Cremorna Garden mention; Cole (Grimsby & Cole) and Challoner. Ch VII: Harriet; plot discussion. Ch VIII: Bunter; Marjorie Phelps; Kropotky party; Joey Trimbles; Sylvia Marriott; Eiluned Price. Ch IX: Bunter & Mrs. Pettican & Hannah tea (crumpets). Ch X: Mrs. Bulfinch; white paper packet (bicarbonate later); Urquhart's office interview; Cremorna Garden's will. Ch XI: Urquhart's will draft (Woodstock typewriter, chipped lower-case p, misaligned A); Murchison letter re Megatherium Trust. Ch XII: Christmas at Duke's Denver; Freddy's Megatherium & Rachel Levy engagement. Ch XIII: Miss Murchison visits Wimsey; Bill Rumm lesson; picklocks. Ch XIV: Miss Murchison opens Wrayburn box; finds Deed of Trust and letter (15 May 1920). Ch XV: Wimsey & Miss Climpson; Parker proposal dialogue; packet = bicarbonate of soda. Ch XVI: Miss Climpson at Windle (Hillside View, Miss Booth). Ch XVII: séance; Ch XVIII: séances; Ch XIX: will found in safe (combination from note B; "Black Book"), Miss Climpson steams open envelope, copies; letter to Wimsey 7 Jan 1930. Ch XX: Murchison finds Megatherium receipts, arsenic packet in hidden cupboard behind panel in Urquhart's office. Ch XXI: marsh test; Marsh test positive for arsenic; Bunter deduces. Ch XXII: Wimsey confronts Urquhart; reveals immunity theory (arsenic in cracked egg in omelette); Urquhart eats arrested. Ch XXIII: Crown withdraws charge; verdict Not Guilty; Wimsey proposes to Harriet ("If she'll have me").

Key clue sequence: arsenic-immunity theory (Urquhart took arsenic regularly; hair/nail arsenic); omelette cracked egg; bottle of water; Wimsey's Holloway visit; Miss Price/Sylvia.

**Notable quotes**: "Strong poison" ballad; "I hold by my Whimsy" (Wimsey family motto); "Be thou as chaste as ice..."; Miss Climpson's boarding-house gossip; "Cattery"; Rule Seven "Always distrust the man who looks you straight in the eyes."

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Adele Doring of the Sunnyside Club" by Grace May North (Gutenberg 62151, © 1919, illustrated Florence Liley Young; Lothrop, Lee & Shepard)

**Dedication:** Margaret Edna Rock and happy-hearted girls 10–15.
**Chapters (33):** I The Sunnyside Club; II Secret Sanctum; III Jolly Scrubbing-Party; IV Adele's Secret; V Pleasant Plans; VI Surprise Party; VII Birthday Feast; VIII More Surprises; IX Mother Goose Play-House; X Preparing for Examinations; XI Vacation Days; XII Fudge Party; XIII Two Dryads; XIV Pine Island; XV Exciting Adventure; XVI More Mystery; XVII Little Bear; XVIII Fish Supper; XIX Trip to City; XX Amanda Brown; XXI Ball Game; XXII King's Highway; XXIII School-Days Again; XXIV House by the Wood; XXV Visit to Poorhouse; XXVI Mystery Solved; XXVII Really Truly Home; XXVIII New Pupil; XXIX Eva Begins New Life; XXX Eva Humiliated; XXXI Something Unexpected; XXXII Happy Meeting; XXXIII Farewell to Orphanage.

**Characters**
- Adele Doring: heroine, 13, president, "Heart's Desire" (to Giant Father); golden-brown braids; black pony Firefly, red cart; birthday 13 in April/May; loves writing verse.
- Giant Father (Mr. Doring, Daniel Doring's son); Mrs. Doring ("Adorable Mother", "mumsie"); Jack Doring (brother, a year older; "Pirate the Terrible"); Kate (Irish cook, "Colleen").
- Sunny Seven/Six: Gertrude Willis ("Trudie", minister's daughter, secretary, writer); Bertha Angel (treasurer, practical; brother Bob Angel, grocer's son); Rosamond Wright ("Rosie", romantic, tatting, scared of ghosts); Doris Drexel (banker's daughter; lives next door; grandmother's pine pillow); Betty Burd (youngest, 11, dark, petite; widowed mother; Uncle George Wainwright; pony Star); Peggy Pierce (Bee Hive department store owner's daughter; brother's silver whistle).
- Eva Dearman: orphan, 13 (birthday same day as Adele), golden hair, blue eyes; father broker; mother dead; uncle Dick Dearman (Bar-X Ranch, Silver Creek, Arizona). Her mother's photo.
- Amanda Brown: surly orphan, black braids; mother singer (promised not to sing in concert halls); later voice lessons.
- Mrs. Friend: matron of Orphans' Home (Lake Road). Miss Donovan: teacher (Seven B). Mr. Pierce, Mr. Drexel, Mr. Willis (parson), Mrs. Burd.
- Madge Peterson (artist, 18, Little Bear Lake Inn; brother Everett, "white water-rat"; car "Pigmy"; illustrates Miss Kimberly's book; Dorchester city, Art Institute). Eric Brownley ("Petey"? Actually Everett calls Eric "Petey"; Eric's foster father Jock Henderson); Little Bear the bear; Fiddler Fritz.
- Roberty-Bob (hunchbacked boy, Madge's "Fairy Godmother"; Muffin kitten).
- Granny Dorset (Sarie Dorset, 70th birthday; purple silk dress with lace); Grandpa Dally ('Lijah Dally); Mr. and Mrs. Quigley (Pa and Betsy/Ma; poorhouse; Mrs. Quigley's cloud proverb); Miss Sally Grackle (miser-like recluse; sister Miranda; Dickerson Road house); the miser (gold piece bag in cabin fireplace; $1000).
- Susetta (Susie) Green; Mrs. Melissa (Cyrus) Green, ex-tavern wife of Mr. Cyrus Green; Restwell estate.
- Dorothy? no. Also Jerry Uncle (Uncle Jerry), Uncle Dixon (Japan bowl, Wistaria).
- Mrs. Pettican? no (that's Book 1). Also Richard Dearman = Eva's uncle.

**Events in order**
1. April: seven girls form Sunnyside Club at Buttercup Meadows; pledge rhyme "We promise to look on the Sunnyside…". Officers: Bertha treasurer, Gertrude secretary, Adele president.
2. Log cabin (sheep-herders' cabin, Lookout Hill; grandfather's land) becomes Secret Sanctum; scrubbing party Saturday; china closet of orange boxes; book-case; mosquito netting; pine pillow; blue bowl.
3. Adele's secret: orphan Eva Dearman crying at orphanage; surprise party for Eva's 13th birthday. Bank hidden under shed floor is found missing; Peggy had moved it to father's safe. Purchases at Bee Hive: 12 silver lockets on chains (pink-lined boxes), six dollars thirty-three cents.
4. Surprise party at orphanage; hay-rack with white horses Jerry and Jingo, driven by Bob Angel; boys as black waiters ("Rastus"); birthday cake with 13 pink candy roses; Amanda's party; Jenny Dixon, Mabel Hicks; Amanda locket red stones.
5. Surprise birthday party for Adele at home (library, expressman box "Stories That Girls Like Best", bird's-eye maple desk, water-color of cabin from Mother, fern from Jolly Pirates, Kate's cake "For my little Colleen"; Rosamond's ring).
6. Mother Goose play-house at orphanage cottage; Betty's Mother Goose box.
7. Exams; Betty passes grammar and spelling; pony Star from Uncle George.
8. Fudge party; ghost (whitewashed tree-trunk at cross-roads).
9. Lookout Hill dryads; Madge Peterson; Little Bear Lake; Pine Island; Eric's hide-out; Eric Brownley is the boy who was raised by Jock Henderson; Little Bear story.
10. Fish supper; car ride with Uncle George Wainwright.
11. Monday Eva's art lessons (Madge); Saturday trip to city; Amanda's birthday; Art Institute; Amanda sings lessons.
12. Ball game: North High vs South High; Eric arrives on horse.
13. Gertrude's composition "The King's Highway"; Roberty-Bob.
14. School resumes; Miss Donovan returns; Granny Dorset party planned; Miss Grackle visited, moves back to house; Quigleys to cottage.
15. Miser's gold found in cabin chimney (chipmunk); $1000 deposited at First National Bank, Sunnyside.
16. Party at Miss Grackle's; Quigleys move in.
17. Susetta Green; invitations refused; Mrs. Green takes Eva as maid (black dress, cap, apron); Adele's visit humiliated; Mrs. Doring offers adoption.
18. Uncle Dick Dearman arrives; Eva leaves with Amanda for Arizona; Adele invited west next summer; Jack escorts to Douglas? (train station).
Ending: "If you are also interested, you can learn the 'next chapter' by reading 'Adele Doring on a Ranch.'" END.

Note: Book 2 style: bright, moralising, many exclamations; dialect used by Grandpa Dally and Mr. Quigley.
